content:
Hello!

I'm a full stack software engineer and a hobby mathematician - got a degree in PHIL and ECON from UMD and always thought I'd venture into academia one day, as my family is full of educators. That remains to be seen!

I've been a wallflower here in Zulip for awhile now. Today Anthropic put up their FLT proof, along with some html documents to help translate it. That shows me that maybe someone can get some value out of my web app I've been building. I hope I can contribute to this lovely community.

https://sorryax.com/

Please let me know if it helps you; if I can improve it for your use case; if you find bugs.

Thanks!

Nick Bulka
The relation of this to Lean is tangential at best

There is a Lean typechecker in the "Verify" tab at the bottom, once you import a proof / repo (nanoda, compiled-for-wasm). Sorryax was built to make an early review stage easier, git repos can add a config line pointing at the URL of their lake env lean4export file. Then send the link to someone to review one layer of verification (up to type checking).

Secondly, it's possible that the more visual piece, the Lean lexer and TeX window mapping, did not land as intended. It is a tool aimed at beginners - Lean seen from two angles, the Lean syntax on the left, a .pdf like experience on the right. That "pdf" dynamically updates as the code and files change, and the benefits are visual. Layout that is impossible on a single line can read closer to the math symbols - for example ∑ .

This helps me improve the early messaging and user experience, thanks for taking a look.
